s: Who founded the journal titled ‘Mooknayak’, meaning ‘Leader of the Voiceless’ or ‘Leader of the Silent’?
x: Mooknayak was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1920. It was his first paper and addressed the concerns of the voiceless.
tq: Use the founder–publication association and distinguish the exact title from similar social-reform journals.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mooknayak — 1920
2. Bahishkrit Bharat — 1927
3. Janata — 1930
4. Prabuddha Bharat — 1956
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The four journals were founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the years shown.
tq: Check each year directly against the publication chronology before selecting the complete combination.

s: Which journal founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was associated with Dalit rights and social reform and was started in 1927?
x: Bahishkrit Bharat was founded by Ambedkar in 1927 and focused on Dalit rights and social reform.
tq: Match the publication’s purpose with its year and founder.

s: Janata was renamed as which of the following after Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s conversion to Buddhism?
x: Janata, listed with the year 1930, was renamed Prabuddha Bharat in 1956 after Ambedkar’s conversion to Buddhism.
tq: Discriminate between closely related journal names by using the renaming relationship.

s: The principal aim of Samata Samaj, founded in 1927, was to promote which of the following?
o: Coordination between Dalits and caste Hindus
Representation of labour unions in the Viceroy’s Council
x: Samata Samaj was founded in 1927 to promote coordination between Dalits and caste Hindus.
tq: Infer the organisation’s purpose from the social relationship it was created to coordinate.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Republican Party of India was planned by Ambedkar but was formed in 1957, after his death. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
tq: Find the organisation whose formation date conflicts with the stated succession chronology.

s: The Independent Labour Party, founded in 1936, primarily represented the interests of which groups?
x: The Independent Labour Party worked for the rights of labourers, Dalits and peasants. It contested the 1937 Bombay elections.
tq: Identify the party through its social base rather than through a similar political organisation.

s: Which of the following books was written by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and formed the basis for his thinking behind the Reserve Bank of India?
x: The Problem of the Rupee, published in 1923, contained ideas that formed the basis for Ambedkar’s thinking behind the Reserve Bank of India.
tq: Connect the economic institution with the specific book concerned with currency and the rupee.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Annihilation of Caste — 1936
2. Thoughts on Pakistan — 1940
3. Who Were the Shudras? — 1946
4. The Untouchables — 1948
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched with Ambedkar’s books and their listed years of publication.
tq: Verify the publication years in ascending order and select the complete correct set.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a work of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
x: Servants of India is not a work of Ambedkar. The other three titles were written by him.
tq: Use the author–work trap by distinguishing Ambedkar’s titles from a similarly associated reformist work.

s: Which book by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar dealt with the origin of the Shudras?
x: Who Were the Shudras?, published in 1946, examined the origin of the Shudras.
tq: Match the title’s subject with the corresponding work rather than relying only on the publication year.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: The Buddha and His Dhamma — Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Servants of India — Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
The Problem of the Rupee — Mahatma Gandhi
x: The Buddha and His Dhamma was written by Ambedkar and published in 1957. Gulamgiri was written by Jyotirao Phule, while the other authorship pairs are incorrect.
tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authorship associations.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar obtained his B.A. degree in 1912 from which institution?
x: Ambedkar obtained his B.A. in 1912 from Elphinstone College affiliated with Bombay University.
tq: Match the degree and year with the institution, keeping college-level and university-level studies distinct.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s education?
x: Ambedkar studied at Columbia University, where he obtained an M.A. and Ph.D. Gray’s Inn awarded the qualification of Barrister-at-law, while Osmania University conferred an honorary D.Litt.
tq: Separate academic degrees, legal qualification and honorary doctorates before matching the institutions.

s: At which institution did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar pursue studies leading to the MSc and DSc, with his thesis relating to The Problem of the Rupee?
x: Ambedkar studied at the London School of Economics and obtained the MSc and DSc qualifications; his thesis was related to The Problem of the Rupee.
tq: Use the degree combination and thesis subject to identify the institution.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the early life of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is correct?
o: He was born in 1895 at Bombay in a Mahar family.
He was born in 1891 at Mhow in a Mahar family.
He was born in 1891 at Pune in a Kshatriya family.
He was born in 1889 at Nagpur in a Brahmin family.
x: Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at Mhow, now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar in Madhya Pradesh, in a Mahar family.
tq: Check the combined year, birthplace and social background rather than one detail alone.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was one of the first Dalit students at which institution?
x: Ambedkar was one of the first Dalit students at Elphinstone High School in Bombay.
tq: Distinguish the early schooling reference from the later higher-education institutions.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: Gandhi attended all three conferences as the sole representative of the Depressed Classes.
Gandhi attended only the First Round Table Conference in 1930.
Gandhi did not attend any Round Table Conference.
Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference in 1931.
x: Mahatma Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference, held in 1931. Ambedkar represented the Depressed Classes at the conferences.
tq: Discriminate between Gandhi’s limited attendance and Ambedkar’s representation at the conferences.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s: At the Second Round Table Conference, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s principal demand for the Depressed Classes was for which of the following?
x: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes at the Second Round Table Conference, leading to a clash with Gandhi.
tq: Identify the specific constitutional demand associated with the debate between Ambedkar and Gandhi.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s: The Communal Award of August 1932 was announced by which British Prime Minister?
x: The Communal Award was announced in August 1932 by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. It provided separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.
tq: Match the constitutional measure with the responsible authority and year.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s: Gandhi’s fast unto death against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes took place at which jail?
x: Gandhi undertook the fast unto death at Yerwada Jail, opposing separate electorates because he feared a permanent division in Hindu society.
tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the Poona Pact episode from other prison-related events.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s: Which one of the following was a feature of the Poona Pact of September 1932?
o: Reserved seats in provincial legislatures were abolished.
The Communal Award was extended to all social groups without change.
Joint electorates were accepted and reserved seats in provincial legislatures were increased from 71 to 148.
Separate electorates for the Depressed Classes were retained without modification.
x: The Poona Pact dropped separate electorates and provided joint electorates with reserved seats for the Depressed Classes, increasing the provincial seats from 71 to 148.
tq: Focus on the contrast between separate and joint electorates and check the numerical change in seats.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s: Who mediated the Poona Pact and signed it on behalf of the caste Hindus?
x: Madan Mohan Malaviya mediated the Poona Pact and signed it on behalf of the caste Hindus.
tq: Use the mediator–signatory association to avoid confusing the Pact with the Communal Award.
sec: Round Table Conferences - attendance, demands, Communal Award, Poona Pact

s:
Consider the following statements about the Poona Pact:
1. It provided for joint electorates.
2. It provided reserved seats in the central legislature.
3. It included fair representation in government services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Poona Pact provided joint electorates, reservation in the central legislature and fair representation of the Depressed Classes in government services.
tq: Check whether the provisions relate to elections, legislatures and services before selecting the complete combination.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as Labour Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council during which period?
x: Ambedkar served as Labour Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council from 1942 to 1946.
tq: Match the office with its specific tenure and distinguish it from his post-Independence ministerial role.
sec: Posts held - Executive Council, first cabinet, resignation

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned from the Union Cabinet in 1951 primarily because which proposal was stalled and diluted?
x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951, on 27 September, when the Hindu Code Bill dealing with women’s rights in inheritance, marriage and divorce was stalled and diluted.
tq: Link the resignation to the specific legislative issue rather than to a general political disagreement.
sec: Posts held - Executive Council, first cabinet, resignation

s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s views or public description?
o: Acceptance of Gandhi’s approach without criticism
x: Ambedkar criticised Gandhi’s approach, including in Annihilation of Caste, and rejected the term ‘Harijan’. ‘Modern Manu’, ‘Messenger of Dalits’ and ‘Educate, Agitate, Organise’ are associated with him.
tq: Find the statement that reverses the documented disagreement between Ambedkar and Gandhi.

s: Which work of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, published in 1945, explicitly dealt with the actions of the Congress and Gandhi towards the Untouchables?
o: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables
x: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables was written by Ambedkar in 1945 and expressed his criticism of Congress and Gandhi’s treatment of the Untouchables.
tq: Match the distinctive title and year with the author’s documented criticism.

s: Why did Mahatma Gandhi oppose separate electorates for the Depressed Classes in 1932?
o: He considered separate electorates a provincial matter alone.
He wanted the Communal Award to apply only to Muslims.
He opposed all forms of political representation for the Depressed Classes.
He feared a permanent split in Hindu society.
x: Gandhi opposed separate electorates because he feared that they would create a permanent split in Hindu society, leading to his fast at Yerwada Jail.
tq: Identify the stated cause behind a political action rather than merely recalling the action itself.

s: The Bole Resolution of 1923 is associated with which issue that later formed the background to the Mahad Satyagraha?
o: Abolishing the salt tax in Bombay
Opening temples to all castes throughout India
Opening public watering places to untouchables
x: The Bole Resolution of the Bombay Legislative Council in 1923 opened public watering places to untouchables. Its implementation formed the background to the Mahad Satyagraha.
tq: Connect the preliminary legal resolution with the specific social issue of access to water.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: Which public facility was declared open to untouchables by the Mahad Municipality in 1924, although the decision remained largely on paper?
x: The Mahad Municipality opened the Chavdar Tank to untouchables in 1924, but the decision was not effectively implemented in practice.
tq: Match the local institution with the precise public-access issue.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: On 20 March 1927, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led a march to the Chavdar Tank primarily to assert which right?
o: The right to form a separate province
The right to establish a Buddhist university
The right to enter the Viceroy’s Executive Council
The right of untouchables to access public water
x: On 20 March 1927, Ambedkar led the Water Satyagraha at the Chavdar Tank to assert the right of untouchables to use a public water source.
tq: Identify the symbolic act and connect it with the social right it asserted.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: The Mahad Satyagraha of 20 March 1927 was organised by which organisation?
x: The Mahad Satyagraha was organised by the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha, Ambedkar’s organisation founded in 1924.
tq: Use the organisation–movement association and distinguish it from Ambedkar’s later political parties.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: What was the symbolic act performed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and his followers at Mahad on 20 March 1927?
o: They drank water from the Chavdar Tank.
x: Ambedkar and his followers drank water from the Chavdar Tank, making the event known as the Water Satyagraha.
tq: Recall the central symbolic action rather than a later event associated with Mahad.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: What action was taken by the upper castes after the Mahad Satyagraha?
o: The Bole Resolution was withdrawn by the Bombay Legislative Council.
The tank was permanently opened to all without opposition.
The Manusmriti was officially adopted by the municipality.
x: After Ambedkar’s followers drank water from the Chavdar Tank, upper castes performed a ritual purification of the tank. A court injunction later stalled the second satyagraha.
tq: Distinguish the reaction of the upper castes from the legal consequence that followed.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: The Manusmriti Dahan at Mahad took place on which date?
x: The public burning of the Manusmriti, known as Manusmriti Dahan, took place at Mahad on 25 December 1927.
tq: Separate the date of the Water Satyagraha from the later symbolic burning at Mahad.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar compared the Mahad Satyagraha with which historical event?
o: The American Declaration of Independence of 1776
x: Ambedkar compared the Mahad Satyagraha with the French National Assembly of 1789.
tq: Match the movement with the specific historical analogy used by its leader.
sec: Mahad Satyagraha - year, issue, symbolic act

s: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha was associated with which one of the following places and years?
x: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha was launched at Nashik in 1930.
tq: Use the place–year pair to distinguish the Kalaram Satyagraha from the Mahad and Siddantham movements.

s: With reference to the Kalaram Temple Satyagraha, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It began on 17 December 1933, with about 15,000 volunteers demanding entry into the temple.
It began on 2 March 1930, with about 15,000 volunteers demanding entry into the temple.
It began on 20 March 2026, with about 15,000 volunteers demanding temple entry.
It began on 2 March 1927, with about 2,000 volunteers demanding access to water.
x: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha began on 2 March 1930, and approximately 15,000 volunteers demanded entry into the temple.
tq: Separate the exact starting date and volunteer strength from the dates and figures associated with other events.

s: The movement against the Khoti system, mentioned in connection with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was associated with which region?
x: The Khoti movement was directed against the landlord system in the Konkan region.
tq: Match the movement with its geographical location rather than with the site of the Kalaram Satyagraha.

s: The Mahad and Kalaram Satyagrahas are significant because they compelled the national movement to confront which social issue?
x: Both movements forced the national movement to confront the practice of untouchability.
tq: Identify the common issue linking two separate satyagrahas.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the response of the Indian National Congress to the issue highlighted by the Mahad and Kalaram Satyagrahas:
1. The national movement was compelled to confront untouchability.
2. The Indian National Congress reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee.
3. The reconstituted subcommittee was associated with Malaviya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: the satyagrahas brought untouchability into sharper focus, and the INC reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Malaviya.
tq: Check whether each statement belongs to the same institutional response before selecting the combined option.

s: Which one of the following best represents the distinction between Gandhi's and Ambedkar's approaches to caste?
o: Gandhi and Ambedkar used the same approach, differing only in their terminology.
Gandhi sought to reform Hinduism, retain varna and use the term 'Harijan', whereas Ambedkar advocated annihilation of caste through law and political power.
Gandhi advocated annihilation of caste through law, whereas Ambedkar sought to retain varna within Hinduism.
Both Gandhi and Ambedkar advocated retention of varna and rejected political action.
x: Gandhi's approach involved reforming Hinduism, retaining varna and using the term 'Harijan'. Ambedkar sought the annihilation of caste through legal and political means.
tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by separating the two reform approaches on their distinctive principles.

s: The Telugu title 'Kula Nirmoolana' is associated with which work of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
x: 'Kula Nirmoolana' is the Telugu rendering of Ambedkar's work 'Annihilation of Caste'.
tq: Discriminate between a translated title and the movements or organisations associated with the same subject.

s: In the context of current relevance, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The centenary of the Kalaram Temple Satyagraha is approaching in 2027.
The centenary of the Mahad Satyagraha is approaching in 2027.
The centenary of the Mahad Satyagraha was observed in 2027.
The bicentenary of the Mahad Satyagraha is approaching in 2027.
x: The Mahad Satyagraha centenary is described as approaching in 2027.
tq: Distinguish centenary from bicentenary and Mahad from Kalaram while handling a future-oriented date.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the comparative significance of the Mahad Satyagraha in relation to the Salt Satyagraha?
o: The Mahad Satyagraha was exclusively a temple-entry movement and had no connection with water.
The Mahad Satyagraha brought the issue of salt before the issue of water.
The Mahad Satyagraha began after the Salt Satyagraha had concluded.
The Mahad Satyagraha brought the issue of water before the issue of salt.
x: The comparative formulation associated with Mahad is that water came before salt, highlighting the earlier importance of access to water in the struggle for social equality.
tq: Test the reversed-order trap by comparing the central issues of two well-known movements.

s: The Social Justice Ministry began a two-year celebration connected with whose 200th birth anniversary?
x: The Social Justice Ministry began a two-year celebration of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary.
tq: Link the ministry initiative with the correct reformer's anniversary rather than with another social-justice leader.

s: Annihilation of Caste, known in Telugu as Kula Nirmoolana, had a notable influence on which of the following?
o: The Khoti landlord system in Konkan
x: Annihilation of Caste inspired Andhra Dalit literature, where it is known as Kula Nirmoolana.
tq: Apply the work–regional influence relationship instead of confusing a literary influence with a political movement or system.

s: Gandhi launched a temple-entry movement at Siddantham in which district and on what date?
x: Gandhi launched temple entry at Siddantham in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
tq: Combine the location and date to distinguish the Siddantham temple-entry action from the Kalaram Satyagraha.
